Within the three first-cycle CALCE slices, DFN measured the lowest mean voltage-shape RMSE (0.0722 V), compared with SPM (0.1709 V) and SPMe (0.2550 V). All three models nevertheless overpredicted absolute capacity by roughly 38-45%; this bounded comparison is not a calibrated validation and does not establish universal model superiority.
Across the three first-cycle CALCE slices, DFN had lower mean voltage-shape RMSE (0.0722 V) than SPM (0.1709 V) and SPMe (0.2550 V), while all three models overpredicted capacity.
The CALCE experiments prove that DFN is universally superior to SPM and SPMe and validate DFN as the best battery model.
